@Arthur Dobelis one big change we made was that Dylan is planning on including cardinality with the column metadata. This will make it so the frontend can contain the logic which will determine if series / x-axis can be swapped, and should reduce the number of "charting scenarios" we have from the backend's perspective down to 3: simple x/y chart, a chart with a column of series groupings, and a chart with multiple metric columns that should be used as individual series. replied to a thread:@here Sprint 4 has ended!

All tickets were completed except adding SQL Server and (stretch goal) file upload support. This means:

HUGE leaps in the quality of our charts and ability to account for complex, multi-series data. Draft blueprint is now created behind the scenes on linking a new ds to the workspace. The blueprint conversation now shows the draft blueprint on load -- much clearer UX. We discussed making this improvement months ago, and it was finally timeMany improvements to our blueprint agent: correcting its understanding of the context of the blueprint task, enabling conversation and blueprint inspection (not just status updates), and enabling the blueprint to be augmented with high-value low-cardinality data (statuses, types, geo regions) so that the query agent doesn't have tho guess filter values. This inspection is performed by the agent, but gated by the user's permission to look at the unique values of those specific columns.Saving and displaying saved assets. Assets save to the right rail of the data explorer conversation. Clicking an asset navigates to its genesis point in the conversation. Basic stub Dashboards & Reports page -- shows a list of saved assets, point of departure for d&r authoring.

Scope changes: we mostly stayed within the original lines of the planned sprint. However:
The data source to blueprint workflow change was a bit of a surprise addition. I kept running into issues with the blueprint flow so I decided to spend some time focusing on this. The bugfix to stop duplicate tables from appearing in the BP became a bit more complex than expected. The bug stemmed from a hard-to-comprehend earlier choice to "normalize" table and column names from Postgres by lowercasing them. You actually can't do that -- PG has no idea what you mean when you ask for the lowercased name. But I naively followed the pattern rather than pulling the normalization code out. This quietly broke the app and required some backtracking to fix. Enabling value inspection was also not in the original sprint plan, but the chart improvements and focus on charts made the limitation of not knowing values much more apparent during data exploration. Basically chart improvements encouraged a lot of focus on the upstream process -- but also small things like adding params to the SQL display.
